LACSON: IMEE MARCOS' DRUG ALLEGATIONS AT RELIGIOUS GATHERING 'UN-FILIPINO'

Senate President Pro Tempore Ping Lacson on Tuesday slammed Sen. Imee Marcos for publicly accusing her brother, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., of drug use during a major religious gathering, calling the act "very un-Filipino" and "unacceptable."

In an interview on True FM, Lacson said that while disagreements among siblings are normal, Filipino culture dictates that such conflicts be resolved privately — not aired before hundreds of thousands of people at a public event.

"Ang masasabi ko lang, medyo napaka un-Filipino. Tayo nakasaksi ng pag-aaway ng magkakapatid pero yan confined sa bahay... Pero magsalita ka sa harap ng daang libong tao sa Luneta, para sa akin, hindi katanggap-tanggap bilang isang Pilipino. Hindi tayo ganyang mga Pilipino," he said.

Lacson added that he was "disappointed" by Marcos' decision to make the allegations at a religious gathering, stressing that accusations — "whether true or not" — should not be hurled in such a venue.

He was referring to Marcos' speech at the Iglesia ni Cristo rally in Manila on Monday evening, where she claimed that the President and members of his family were involved in drug use.

When asked about the senator's possible motivations, Lacson was blunt: "Pulitika, wala namang iba. Wala akong makitang motibo. Bakit mo sisiraan ang sarili mong kapatid sa harap ng daan daang libong tao?"
